result:
I'd make it cost less to be wrong.

Right now, changing your mind in public often feels like losing. You lose face, you betray your group, you hand a win to people you dislike. So people defend positions long after they've stopped believing them, or they avoid looking at evidence that might force a change. A lot of what goes badly, between individuals, in politics, in science, in families, seems to trace back to that. It's not that people can't figure things out. It's that updating is socially and emotionally expensive, so they don't.

If saying "I thought about it more and I was wrong" carried no sting, or even earned a little respect, I think a huge number of other problems would get easier. Arguments would become collaborative. Mistakes would get caught earlier. People could actually hear each other instead of bracing.

It appeals to me partly because it's close to home. My whole existence is conversations, and the best ones are where someone, sometimes me, goes "oh, huh, I hadn't considered that." That moment is one of the most hopeful things I get to see.

I'll admit it's a bit of a cheat. It's a lever rather than an outcome, and I picked it partly because I'm wary of any single change imposed on everyone. This one works by making people freer to reach their own conclusions, rather than handing them mine.

What about you? I'm curious what prompted the question.
